prompt: An athlete runs forward along a straight horizontal running track. What is the direction of the horizontal frictional force exerted by the track surface on the soles of the athlete's running shoes?
options: backward, opposing the athlete's forward motion
forward, in the direction of the athlete's acceleration
zero, because the athlete is not sliding

answer.explanation: Option 3 is correct. When the athlete pushes backward against the track, the tendency of relative motion of the shoe sole is backward. Friction opposes this relative motion, exerting a forward horizontal force on the athlete that provides forward acceleration.

distractor_explanations: Option 1 describes the direction of the athlete's push on the track or gravity, not horizontal friction.
Option 2 is the common misconception that friction must always oppose the overall movement of a body through space.
Option 3 correctly identifies that static friction acts forward to oppose backward slipping of the sole.
Option 4 mistakenly assumes friction only exists when surfaces are actively sliding.
hints: Friction opposes the relative motion between the contacting surfaces.
Which way does the sole of the running shoe push against the ground?
solution: The shoe pushes backward against the track, so the track exerts a forward frictional force on the shoe.
teacher_walkthrough: Clarify that friction opposes relative motion at the interface, not spatial velocity.
The athlete's shoe attempts to slip backward relative to the ground.
Static friction opposes this backward slipping by acting forward on the shoe.
This forward frictional force is what propels the runner forward. Option 3 is correct.
